draft.title: Exponential and logarithmic equations
card: Same base
If both sides can be written with the same base, equate the indices. Example: 2^(x+1) = 32 = 2⁵, so x + 1 = 5 and x = 4.
Take logs
If the bases cannot match, take logs of both sides. Example: 3^x = 20 gives x = log₃(20) = log(20) ÷ log(3), which is about 2.73.
Log equations
Combine the logs into one using the log laws, then rewrite in index form. Example: log₂(x) + log₂(x − 2) = 3 gives log₂(x(x − 2)) = 3, so x² − 2x = 8.
Domain check
A log needs a positive input. Test each answer in the original equation. For x² − 2x = 8, x = 4 or x = −2. Only x = 4 works, as log₂(−2) is undefined.
draft.remember: Match the base or take logs, then check every answer against the log's domain.

a.why: 81 = 3⁴, so 2x = 4 and x = 2. Choosing x = 4 comes from stopping at the index 4 and forgetting to divide by 2.
a.clue: Write 81 as a power of 3, then equate the indices.

b.why: Combining gives x(x − 6) = 27, so x² − 6x − 27 = 0 and (x − 9)(x + 3) = 0. The input of a log must be positive, so x = −3 is rejected and only x = 9 remains. Giving both values skips the domain check.
b.clue: Test each solution in the original equation.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's worked examples are correct, and both questions have a single right answer (x = 2 and x = 9) that matches the explanations.

final.title: Exponential and logarithmic equations
card: Same base
If both sides can be written with the same base, equate the indices. Example: \(2^{x + 1} = 32 = 2^{5}\), so \(x + 1 = 5\) and \(x = 4\).
Take logs
If the bases cannot match, take logs of both sides. Example: \(3^{x} = 20\) gives \(x = \log_{3} 20 = \frac{\log_{e} 20}{\log_{e} 3}\), which is about 2.73.
Log equations
Combine the logs into one using the log laws, then rewrite in index form. Example: \(\log_{2}(x) + \log_{2}(x - 2) = 3\) gives \(\log_{2}(x(x - 2)) = 3\), so \(x^{2} - 2x = 8\).
Domain check
A log needs a positive input. Test each answer in the original equation. For \(x^{2} - 2x = 8\), \(x = 4\) or \(x = -2\). Only \(x = 4\) works, as \(\log_{2}(-2)\) is undefined.
final.remember: Match the base or take logs, then check every answer against the log's domain.

a.clue: Write 81 as a power of 3, then equate the indices.

b.why: Combining gives \(x(x - 6) = 27\), so \(x^{2} - 6x - 27 = 0\) and \((x - 9)(x + 3) = 0\). The input of a log must be positive, so \(x = -3\) is rejected and only \(x = 9\) remains. Giving both values skips the domain check.
b.clue: Test each solution in the original equation.
